newsitem.title: UK: BFI extends decline in sloppy dry cargo market.
newsitem.headline: BFI extends decline in sloppy dry cargo market.

text.p: The Baltic Freight Index (BFI) extended its new decline on Tuesday by six to 1085 points in a dry cargo freight market depressed by prompt available tonnage.
The BFI has dropped steadily from 1119 that was reached 10 days ago on a rebound from the August 8 four-year low of 1060, which brokers said could now soon be tested again.
BIFFEX futures were by contrast higher on Tuesday with most traded October up 27 at 1235 in volume of 297 lots by 1615 GMT.
"The move is technical and it is not driven by any higher prices in the cash market", said a broker.
The few fixtures that were reported were generally sideways on Tuesday.
Among Panamaxes in the grains trade, Korean charterers were reported to have fixed US Gulf/Japan no combination at $19.75.
"But the majors are not seen much at the moment", a broker said, adding that the recent build-up of tonnage in the US Gulf required a big volume of business to soak it up.
Timecharters included Panocean fixing 1981-built Evgenia 69,637 dwt delivery US Gulf 7/8 September trip redelivery South Korea at $10,250 daily plus $150,000 bonus.
